subject: Agriculture
title: Pesticide Poisoning
description: A fast breakdown of Pesticide Poisoning for builders.

hook.text: 385 million cases of acute pesticide poisoning occur worldwide each year. Most victims are poor farmers.

buildup.text: In developing countries, farmers spray without protective equipment—bare hands, no masks, sandals.

discovery.text: Organophosphate pesticides—designed to attack insect nervous systems—do the same to human nerves.

twist.text: Many banned pesticides in Europe are still manufactured there and exported to developing countries for use.

climax.text: Pesticide self-poisoning is a leading method of suicide in rural Asia—killing 150,000 people annually.

punchline.text: The chemicals meant to protect food are killing the farmers who grow it.

quiz.question: How many cases of acute pesticide poisoning occur worldwide each year?

details.summary: Pesticide poisoning affects an estimated 385 million agricultural workers each year, with 11,000 annual fatalities. This topic covers how farmworkers are exposed, the acute and chronic health effects of different pesticide classes, and what can be done to reduce poisoning.
details.whyItMatters: Pesticide poisoning is one of the largest occupational health crises in the world, disproportionately affecting workers in developing countries. Reducing poisoning requires better regulation, training, protective equipment, and less toxic.
takeaways: An estimated 385 million cases of pesticide poisoning occur among farmworkers annually
Organophosphates and carbamates cause acute neurotoxicity and can be fatal in minutes
Developing countries account for the vast majority of pesticide poisoning deaths

faq.question: How are farmworkers typically exposed to dangerous pesticides?
faq.answer: Exposure occurs through skin contact during mixing and spraying, inhalation of spray drift, contaminated clothing, re-entering treated fields too soon, and drinking water contaminated by runoff. In developing countries, lack of protective equipment dramatically increases risk.

faq.question: What are the long-term health effects of chronic pesticide exposure?
faq.answer: Chronic exposure is linked to increased rates of cancer (particularly lymphoma and leukemia), neurological disorders including Parkinson's disease, reproductive problems, hormonal disruption, respiratory diseases, and developmental effects in children of exposed workers.
